rationale: One real defect: sanitize_args strips only args matching a secret-flag regex, so other secret-bearing args (positional tokens, -H Authorization, --auth/--bearer/--credential) are cloned verbatim and unreported. No defers; 23 candidates dismissed as noise or accepted by design (name race, no locking) or unreachable (None headers/env/args are non-nullable fields). Not every dismissed candidate was individually traced to source, so confidence is medium.

findings.title: Args secrets stripped only by flag-name regex
findings.problem: sanitize_args blanks a value only when the arg matches _FLAG_WITH_VALUE_RE or follows a flag-only arg whose name contains token/api-key/password/passwd/secret/key. Positional tokens, '-H Authorization: ...' header args, connection strings or URLs with credentials in args, and flags such as --auth, --bearer, --credential are copied verbatim into the clone and are not reported in stripped_fields. The route docstring and the task decision state that secrets in args are replaced with placeholders by default.
findings.impact: A clone created without copy_values can carry secrets from args in plaintext, and the clone may be public because is_public is copied. The caller is also not told via stripped_fields that these values were left in place. Reachability confirmed by reading sanitize_args and sanitize_config: no other path touches args.
findings.recommendation: Widen the secret-word set (auth, bearer, credential, pwd, authorization), run arg values containing '://' through sanitize_url, blank values of '-H'/'--header' args, and report every blanked index in stripped_fields. Alternatively blank all args by default, keeping flag names, and let copy_values opt back in by args[<i>].
